sources.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension
sources.version_or_commit: Living official SQLite documentation accessed 2026-10-12; contentless-delete tables documented since SQLite 3.43.0; shipped application runtime remains unknown.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1, 3, 4.3.1–4.3.4, 4.4.1–4.4.4, 6.12–6.13; FTS build availability, query grammar, Unicode61/trigram, contentless and contentless-delete operations, external-content synchronization, rebuild and secure-delete.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened the official FTS5 documentation at the tokenizer, table-mode, rebuild and secure-delete sections; checked the 3.43.0 contentless-delete condition, ordinary contentless UPDATE/DELETE restrictions, all-columns UPDATE rule, rebuild limitation, tokenizer defaults and deleted-term retention.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: unicode61 is the default and based on Unicode 6.1; letter/number/private-use runs are tokens, punctuation/space separate, and Latin diacritics are removed by default. Ordinary contentless tables do not support ordinary UPDATE/DELETE; their special delete command uses original indexed values and rowid. Since SQLite 3.43.0, contentless-delete tables support DELETE and INSERT OR REPLACE, and UPDATE only when all user-defined columns are supplied; they do not support the special delete command. External-content data is in the same database and synchronization is caller responsibility. Rebuild deletes/recreates the whole index and is unavailable for contentless tables. FTS5 postings may retain deleted terms until merge unless secure-delete is enabled.
sources.applicability: Primary source for conditional FTS5 design, tokenizer language limits, contentless CRUD and rebuild decisions, and at-rest posting caveat. Verify the actual runtime/build and tokenizer/index mode before implementation.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Living official SQLite documentation; WAL available since SQLite 3.7.0.
sources.locator: Sections 1, 2, 2.1–2.3; concurrency, checkpointing, filesystem and attached-database conditions.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened official WAL documentation and checked reader/writer concurrency, one-writer limit, same-host/network-filesystem condition, checkpoint behavior and multi-database atomicity note.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows readers and a writer concurrently, but there is still only one writer at a time. Processes must use the database on one host; WAL does not work over a network filesystem. Transactions changing multiple attached database files are atomic per file but not across the set under WAL; long readers can hold back checkpoint progress.
sources.applicability: Relevant only if the target notebook or index uses SQLite/WAL; supports measuring same-database edit contention and keeping the canonical outbox durable across a separate index commit.

sources.title: SQLite ATTACH DATABASE
sources.version_or_commit: Living official SQLite documentation, last updated 2025-02-06 per page.
sources.locator: Transactions involving multiple attached databases, section 2, paragraph on commit atomicity.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official ATTACH documentation and checked the atomicity exception for WAL or an in-memory main database.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cross-database transactions are atomic as a set when main is not :memory: and journal_mode is not WAL. Under WAL or an in-memory main database, each file remains individually atomic, but a host crash during multi-file commit may leave files inconsistent.
sources.applicability: Supports the conservative outbox rule if a sidecar is a separate SQLite database; does not establish that the target app uses ATTACH or WAL.

sources.title: SQLite forum/maintainer record: external-content FTS5 with nested AFTER UPDATE writes
sources.version_or_commit: Report dated 2026-08-04/05; report names SQLite 3.45.1, 3.45.3 and 3.53.2 reproductions; status Resolved; no release fix identified in the record.
sources.locator: Corrected reproducer and workaround, posts/sections describing a standard external-content FTS sync trigger plus a second same-table AFTER UPDATE trigger that performs a nested UPDATE.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened the corrected maintainer/forum record; checked the minimal trigger combination, named tested versions, report scope, and suggested workaround.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The report is conditional on an external-content FTS5 sync trigger plus another AFTER UPDATE trigger on the same content table that performs a nested UPDATE; the report describes content/data-dependent reproduction. The workaround is to avoid the nested same-table trigger write or fold its mutation into the original update. It is not evidence that all external-content FTS5 trigger designs fail.
sources.applicability: If evaluating external-content FTS5, inspect and test the actual complete trigger graph and shipped SQLite runtime; treat this as a conditional issue report, not a general product defect.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 IndexWriter API
sources.locator: IndexWriter add_document, delete_term, commit and run documentation.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened version-pinned API docs at commit/delete visibility and blocking conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: commit blocks and publishes/persists pending documents; deletes become visible on commit; add_document and run may block when the indexing pipeline is full. The API's indexed opstamp can align client queues with commits.
sources.applicability: Supports a bounded background writer and post-commit acknowledgement proposal; actual target workload, OS support and UI latency remain to be tested.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 tokenizer module
sources.locator: Default, en_stem, custom tokenizer and SimpleTokenizer sections.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened version-pinned tokenizer docs and checked default split/lowercase/long-token behavior, English stemmer behavior, and custom tokenizer registration.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The default tokenizer splits on whitespace/punctuation, lowercases and drops tokens longer than 40 characters. en_stem adds English stemming and is slower. Custom tokenizer/filter registration is supported; these facts do not establish language quality for the target scripts.
sources.applicability: Supports qualified tokenizer comparison and the requirement to fixture indexing and query parsing for each declared script.

sources.title: Tantivy 0.26.2 deleting/updating documents example
sources.version_or_commit: Repository tag 0.26.2, as named by the version-pinned URL.
sources.locator: Lines 561–600 for ID field and primary-ID limitation; 656–708 for delete plus reinsert, commit and reader reload.
sources.observed_operation: Reopened the version-pinned library example source and checked its stable indexed ID, lack of enforced primary-key uniqueness, delete-plus-reinsert update, commit, and reader reload.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The example states Tantivy has no primary-ID notion and does not enforce uniqueness. It demonstrates an app-indexed ID and update by delete_term plus reinsert, visible to clients after commit and reader reload.
sources.applicability: Supports treating uniqueness and canonical source synchronization as app responsibilities and storing only fields permitted by the notebook's source-of-truth rule; this is library sample code, not target application code.
